'''Gail Alexandra Carpenter''' is an American [[Cognitive science|cognitive scientist]], [[neuroscientist]] and [[mathematician]], known for her work with [[Stephen Grossberg]] developing [[adaptive resonance theory]], a theory of how the human brain [[information processing theory|processes information]], and for her work on the [[Hodgkin–Huxley model]] of how [[neuron]]s operate.<ref name=fellow/>

She is a [[professor emerita]] of mathematics and statistics at [[Boston University]],<ref name=echo/> where she was also a professor of cognitive and neural systems.<ref name=fellow/>

==Education and career==
Carpenter attended the [[International School of Geneva]]<ref name=echo>{{cite web|url=https://issuu.com/feig/docs/echo_28/s/16549411|title=Les Scientifiques|work=Echo magazine|volume=28|date=Summer 2022|publisher=International School of Geneva|via=Issuu|access-date=2025-06-21}}</ref> then went to the [[University of Colorado]].<ref name=fellow/> She completed her Ph.D. in mathematics in 1975 at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], with the dissertation ''Traveling Wave Solutions of Nerve Impulse Equations'' supervised by [[Charles C. Conley]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|9265}}</ref>

Carpenter was a faculty member at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and at [[Northeastern University]] before joining Boston University.<ref name=brief/>

==Recognition==
Carpenter was the first woman to receive the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE) Neural Networks Pioneer Award in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cis.ieee.org/awards/past-recipients#NeuralNetworksPioneerAward|title=Past recipients: Neural Networks Pioneer Award|publisher=IEEE|access-date=2025-06-21}}</ref><ref name=brief>{{cite magazine|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/4442248|magazine=IEEE Computational Intelligence Magazine|title=Society Briefs: 2008 CIS Awards|first=Enrique|last=Rusipini|page=4|date=February 2008}}</ref> She received the International Neural Network Society (INNS) Gabor Award in 1999.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.inns.org/inns-award-recipients|title=INNS Award Recipients|publisher=International Neural Network Society|access-date=2025-06-21}}</ref>

She is a Fellow of the INNS,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.inns.org/fellows-senior-members|title=Fellows and senior members|publisher=International Neural Network Society|access-date=2025-06-21}}</ref> and was named as an [[IEEE Fellow]] in 2013.<ref name=fellow>{{cite web|url=https://www.bu.edu/articles/2013/gail-carpenter-named-ieee-fellow/|title=Gail Carpenter Named IEEE Fellow|date=January 29, 2013|first=Amy|last=Laskowski|work=BU Today|publisher=Boston University|access-date=2025-06-21}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Carpenter married [[Stephen Grossberg]] in 1979.<ref>{{cite news|via=Newspapers.com|newspaper=The Jackson Hole Guide|date=June 21, 1979|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/317801978/?article=793bcdc8-8859-426f-a1ad-06890f4299c4&focus=0.036960505,0.094845355,0.2794417,0.50327265&xid=3398|title=Carpenter wed|access-date=2025-06-21}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*Carpenter, G. A. (2019). Looking to the future: Learning from experience, averting catastrophe. Neural Networks. 
*Carpenter, G. A., & Grossberg, S. (1987). A massively parallel architecture for a self-organizing neural pattern recognition machine. Computer Vision, Graphics and Image Processing, 37(1), 54–115. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0734-189X(87)80014-2 
*Carpenter, G. A., Grossberg, S., Markuzon, N., Reynolds, J. H., & Rosen, D. B. (1992). Fuzzy ARTMAP: A Neural Network Architecture for Incremental Supervised Learning of Analog Multidimensional Maps. IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks, 3(5), 698–713. https://doi.org/10.1109/72.159059 
*Carpenter, G. A., Grossberg, S., & Reynolds, J. H. (1991). ARTMAP: Supervised real-time learning and classification of nonstationary data by a self-organizing neural network. Neural Networks, 4(5), 565–588. https://doi.org/10.1016/0893-6080(91)90012-T 
*Carpenter, G. A., Grossberg, S., & Rosen, D. B. (1991). Fuzzy ART: Fast stable learning and categorization of analog patterns by an adaptive resonance system. Neural Networks, 4(6), 759–771. https://doi.org/10.1016/0893-6080(91)90056-B
